Add Student IDs from a Master List

Source: R/student_matching.R
add_student_ids_from_previous.Rd

Reuses existing OME_ID values from a Student Master List by matching students in a new class list.

Matching is attempted first using UPN. Remaining students are matched by name within the same establishment using OMELink::match_person_to_data(), with an exact-name fallback if OMELink is unavailable.

Column names in the class list are resolved using the package's column configuration. Master-list column names are specified independently using master_columns.

Usage

add_student_ids_from_previous(
  new_class_list,
  master_list,
  master_columns = c(ome_id = "OME_ID", sfn = "FNS", sln = "LNS", dob = "DOBS", upn =
    "UPN", est_id = "EST_ID"),
  school_id_column = "est_id",
  verbose = FALSE,
  fuzzy_match = TRUE,
  max_dist = 2,
  method = "osa"
)

Arguments

new_class_list

Current class-list data frame.

master_list

Student Master List data frame.

master_columns

Named character vector mapping internal field names to columns in the master list. By default, FNS and LNS contain historical names separated by "—".

school_id_column

Internal or configured school identifier in the class list. Defaults to "est_id".

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, displays progress information.

fuzzy_match

Logical. If TRUE, performs name matching for remaining unmatched students. Defaults to TRUE.

max_dist

Maximum edit distance passed to OMELink::match_person_to_data().

method

Matching method passed to OMELink::match_person_to_data().

Value

Updated class list containing OME_ID, MATCH_METHOD, OLD_STUDENT_FIRST_NAME, OLD_STUDENT_LAST_NAME and OLD_DOB.

Details

The original matching methodology is retained. UPN matching uses match(), taking the first matching master-list record. Name-based matching is restricted to the selected school.

OLD_STUDENT_FIRST_NAME and OLD_STUDENT_LAST_NAME are always returned in lowercase. For UPN matches, these contain the complete historical name strings from FNS and LNS. For OMELink matches, they contain the matched name candidates.

Historical DoBs separated by "—" are considered individually when checking for mismatches for fuzzy/partial name matches.

Additional master-list fields are not used in matching.
